roundRock.ruling_applied: Operator-ruled 2026-09-07 (relayed via dispatch), applied verbatim: side_corner_ft uses the corpus's Section-1-50 front-lot-line derivation (not the base-side-mirror assumption); district breadth widened to 10 (was 4 in corpus); SF-3's side_ft/rear_ft REFUSED (two genuinely different, GIS-code-indistinguishable ordinance sub-columns), not picked; max_height_ft sentinel unified to 999 (was split 100/999 across the two source tables).
roundRock.extension_beyond_ruling: The ruling covered the 4 districts both source tables shared (SF-R/SF-1/SF-2/SF-3). Applied the same Section-1-50 derivation to the 6 legacy-design-tools-only districts (MH, TF, TH, SR, MF-1, MF-2), since Sec. 1-50 is a general Chapter 1 rule, not Article-II-single-family-specific -- reported to doc-repo-26 rather than assumed, and separately ruled on.
roundRock.second_review_correction: TH's side_corner_ft was corrected from 5 to 20: the file's own pre-existing provenance quote already named 20 ft as the directly-tabulated adjacent-to-street value, but the stored numeric field read 5 (mirroring side_ft) -- a data/quote mismatch bug, not a re-derivation.
roundRock.mf2_ruling: Second-review finding (this lane) + operator ruling (doc-repo-26, relayed): MF-2 is the only district where front_ft (15) < side_ft (25), so applying the derivation would LOOSEN the corner setback from the superseded 25 to a derived 15 -- the dangerous direction. Ruled: a derivation is trustworthy when it tightens a figure and insufficient on its own when it loosens one. MF-2's side_corner_ft is REFUSED (not_specified: true, 25 -- the conservative candidate -- carried as a required-by-schema placeholder), with a quote naming the citation search that found no primary source for a distinct value.
roundRock.gate_enforcement: New gate rule G7 (hauska-setback-corpus's ported gate.ts) BLOCKS any max_height_ft flagged not_specified whose value is not the canonical 999 -- machine-checked, not a convention, proven by a synthetic test seeding the old 100 sentinel.
files: both repos' schema.json (unrelated pre-existing drift fixed: atom_did wrongly required, primary-source-verified missing from the enum)

kyleRegression.finding: Confirmed at source in hauska-setback-corpus's kyle-tx.json (9 districts) and legacy-design-tools' own kyle-tx.json (identical, confirmed to be the actual un-fixed source the 2026-09-07 14:09 UTC corpus merge took): every field on every district carried verification_state human-verified or asserted with atom_did='kyle_tx/ch53/53-33', a fabricated citation -- kyle_tx has zero real code-section atoms (confirmed live against the atoms store by hauska-engine PR #393, which fixed this same fabrication for 5 districts fourteen hours before the merge silently reverted it and extended it onto 4 more).
kyleRegression.fix: All 9 districts x 7 fields relabeled to primary-source-verified, every atom_did removed, in both the corpus and legacy-design-tools' own copy. hauska-engine's frozen-baseline kyle-tx.json (5 districts, already correct since #393) deliberately left untouched -- its retirement is a separate, later step per the divergence test's own docstring.
kyleRegression.gate_enforcement: New gate.ts test seeds the literal atom_did 'kyle_tx/ch53/53-33' against an empty atom set and asserts G2 BLOCKS it -- the actual fabricated citation, not a stand-in.

divergenceTest.bug_found: hauska-engine's corpus-divergence.test.ts iterated `for (const vendoredDistrict of vendored.districts)` (one-directional: corpus-only districts, like Kyle's 4 unreviewed additions, were never examined) and its own docstring explicitly excluded verification_state/confidence/atom_did/quote from comparison -- both halves of the Kyle regression landed exactly in that blind spot.
divergenceTest.fix: Refactored into an exported pure function `compareTables` checked in both directions (set equality on district names) plus provenance monotonicity (verification_state must not weaken). The monotonicity rank is deliberately non-obvious -- primary-source-verified ranks ABOVE human-verified here, documented inline, because human-verified has now shipped fabricated twice in this corpus (Round Rock's original correction, this Kyle regression) while primary-source-verified is the earned ceiling for a confirmed-zero-atom jurisdiction; under the naive ranking the Kyle regression would NOT be flagged as a 'weakening'.
divergenceTest.proof_by_violation: 6 new synthetic tests against `compareTables` directly (not the npm package): identical tables pass; an extra unreviewed district fails; a weakened verification_state fails (the Kyle shape); both together are both caught in one run; a legitimate strengthening (asserted -> primary-source-verified) does not false-positive; the reviewed Kyle/Round-Rock district-count allowlist entries do not false-positive.
divergenceTest.known_asymmetry_allowlist: Kyle's 4 GIS-frequency-added districts and Round Rock's 6 newly-widened districts are explicit, dated, reasoned entries (not a silent pass, not a permanently-red gate per DEV_PROCESS 2.0) -- any future unreviewed addition still fails.

LESSON: a provenance/trust-state 'monotonicity' rank is not always the intuitively 'stronger label wins' ordering -- when a label has been caught fabricated in this specific corpus more than once (human-verified, twice), the correct rank for a regression-detection test reflects which state that corpus has learned to distrust, not the state's nominal claim strength. Document the inversion inline or a future reader will 'fix' it back to the wrong order.
